name: TiKV
tagline: CNCF-graduated, Raft-replicated transactional key-value store in Rust; the storage layer of TiDB.
description: TiKV is a distributed key-value database that splits an ordered keyspace into Raft-replicated regions and offers both raw and Percolator-style distributed ACID transactions. PingCAP built it as the storage engine for TiDB and donated it to the CNCF, where it graduated in 2020; it can also be used standalone, for example as the backend for JuiceFS metadata or Redis-protocol layers. A Placement Driver handles timestamps, scheduling and rebalancing. It is a strong fit when you need a horizontally scalable, strongly consistent KV store and are comfortable running a multi-component cluster.

pricing.notes: Free; commercial support and TiDB Cloud (which includes TiKV) from PingCAP.

scale.notes: Automatic region splitting and balancing via PD; multi-PB TiDB/TiKV clusters are documented. Placement rules and follower reads support cross-region layouts.

strengths: Distributed ACID transactions with snapshot isolation across regions of keyspace
Raft replication with automatic failover and rebalancing
Written in Rust on RocksDB, with years of production hardening under TiDB
Raw API for maximum throughput when transactions are not needed
MVCC enables stale and historical reads
weaknesses: Needs Placement Driver and several TiKV nodes; heavy for small deployments
Timestamp oracle adds latency for globally distributed writes
Standalone (non-TiDB) client ecosystem is thinner than TiDB's
Tuning RocksDB and Raft parameters takes expertise
useCases: Redis-protocol or custom data layers needing strong consistency
